title: High-Quality Single-Cell RNA-Seq from Tissue Sections with DRaqL
author: Ikeda, Miyao, et al.

steps.title: Prepare RNase‑free workspace
steps.instruction: Set up a clean RNase‑free area using RNase‑free 10‑µL, 200‑µL and 1000‑µL tips, tubes and PCR tubes, high‑quality distilled water, disposable gloves and surgical masks; decontaminate surfaces with RNase Quiet or RNase ZAP and handle tube caps with two hands to avoid touching the inside.

steps.title: Prepare frozen ovaries
steps.instruction: Snap‑freeze mouse ovaries and embed them for sectioning.

substeps.instruction: Place liquid nitrogen in a Styrofoam box or Dewar vessel.
Humanely sacrifice an 8‑week‑old female mouse and excise the ovaries.
Remove as much ovarian fat pad as possible with tweezers and surgical scissors.
Wash excised ovaries in 1× PBS.
Chill embedding medium (10 % PVA/1× PBS) or OCT in a cryomold on ice.
Quickly freeze the ovaries by submerging them in liquid nitrogen.
Embed the frozen ovaries in the chilled medium and immediately return to liquid nitrogen.
Store the embedded ovaries at –80 °C.

steps.title: Stain frozen ovarian sections
steps.instruction: Apply Cresyl violet (and optional Eosin Y) staining, wash, and dry the sections before LCM.

substeps.instruction: Place membrane slides with frozen sections on a paper towel at 25 °C.
Apply 500 µL of 0.1 %–1 % Cresyl violet acetate in 50 % isopropanol (typically 1 % Cresyl violet/50 % isopropanol) to the sections and let stand for 30 s at 25 °C.
Discard excess staining solution by tilting the slide over the paper towel.
Optional: stain with 0.17 % Eosin Y in 60 % ethanol for 50 s at 25 °C, then discard excess as above.
Wash the slide once with 50 %–100 % isopropanol (or 50 %–100 % ethanol as an alternative).
Air‑dry the slide for 1 h at 25 °C.
Pause point: slides can be stored at –80 °C for ≥6 months in a slide mailer inside a Ziploc bag with 5 g blue silica‑gel; before LCM, warm stepwise (–20 °C 10 min → 4 °C 10 min → 25 °C).

steps.title: Purify amplified cDNA with magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Use AxyPrep MAG PCR Clean‑up Kit (or equivalent SPRI beads) to clean up the amplified cDNA.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 70 % ethanol (14 mL dH₂O + 6 mL ethanol) in a 50 mL nuclease‑free tube and set up a DynaMag‑2 magnetic stand.
Add 20 µL paramagnetic bead solution (~0.8× the cDNA volume) to a 1.5‑mL tube at 25 °C.
Add the cDNA sample (product of Step 30) to the beads, mix, and incubate 5 min at 25 °C.
Place tubes on the magnetic stand for 3 min; once cleared, remove supernatant.
Add 200 µL 70 % ethanol, mix, incubate 30 s at 25 °C, then magnetic stand 3 min and remove supernatant.
Repeat the ethanol wash once more.
Briefly centrifuge to collect residual ethanol, place on magnetic stand, and remove all remaining ethanol with a pipette.
Elute DNA by adding 50 µL dH₂O, vortex to resuspend beads, and incubate 3 min on the magnetic stand.
Transfer the clear supernatant (purified cDNA) to a new tube.
Pause point: store purified cDNA at ≤ –20 °C for ≥1 year.

steps.title: Library preparation for 3′‑end sequencing
steps.instruction: Pool IL‑indexed cDNAs, perform tagmentation with Nextera XT, amplify with indexed PCR primers, and clean up the library.

substeps.instruction: Pool cDNA samples that carry different in‑line (IL) indexes (typically 1 µL or 0.2 ng per sample).
Measure total cDNA amount; if concentration < 0.1 ng/µL, concentrate using 0.8× AxyPrep beads (see purification steps).
Dilute pooled cDNA to 60–800 pg/µL.
Thaw Nextera XT reagents: Tagment DNA Buffer, Amplicon Tagment Mix, and nuclease‑free water.
On ice, prepare 20 µL tagmentation mix: 10 µL Tagment DNA Buffer, 5 µL Amplicon Tagment Mix, 5 µL water, and 0.5–5 µL mixed cDNA (300–400 pg).
Run tagmentation: 50 °C 5 min, then hold at 10 °C indefinitely; place tubes on ice afterward.
Add 5 µL Neutralize Tagment Buffer, mix gently, brief centrifuge, then incubate 25 °C 5 min; keep on ice.
Thaw Nextera PCR Master Mix, Tn Forward PCR primer (P5 index, 10 µM) and Reverse PCR primer (P7 index, 10 µM); keep on ice.
Prepare 25 µL PCR master mix on ice: 15 µL Nextera PCR Master Mix, 1 µL Reverse PCR primer, 1 µL Tn Forward PCR primer, 8 µL nuclease‑free water.
Add the 25 µL PCR master mix to the neutralized tagmentation product (total 45 µL).
Run PCR: 72 °C 3 min; 95 °C 30 s; 12 cycles of 95 °C 10 s, 55 °C 30 s, 72 °C 30 s; final extension 72 °C 5 min; hold 10 °C.
Pause point: store amplified libraries at ≤ –20 °C for ≤ 1 week.
Purify libraries: add 30 µL AxyPrep beads (~0.6× volume) to each tube at 25 °C, then follow the ethanol‑wash procedure described in the cDNA purification steps (Steps 31‑39).
Elute purified library in 12 µL dH₂O.

steps.title: Prepare and run sequencing
steps.instruction: Quantify, pool, and sequence the indexed libraries on an Illumina platform.

substeps.instruction: Quantify each library with a Qubit 4 Fluorometer using the dsDNA HS Assay kit.
Normalize libraries to the same concentration and pool them at equal molarity (ensure each has a unique P5 and P7 index).
Prepare a 7:3 mixture of the pooled library DNA and PhiX Control v3 DNA to a final loading concentration of 1.6 pM (e.g., 910 µL 1.6 pM library + 390 µL 1.6 pM PhiX = 1400 µL total).
Load the mixture onto a NextSeq 500/550 High‑Output Kit v2.5 (75 cycles).
Run paired‑end sequencing with read 1 = 68 cycles, read 2 = 8 cycles, index 1 = 8 cycles, index 2 = 8 cycles (use 18‑cycle read 2 if UMIs are employed).
Aim for 1–2 million reads per sample.
Post‑run analysis: demultiplex in‑line indexes, perform QC with FASTQC and Fastp, optionally extract UMIs with umi_tools (dedup option), and generate gene counts with htseq‑count (or featureCounts).

description: DRaqL (direct RNA recovery and quenching for laser capture microdissection) allows high-quality RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) for single cells isolated from fixed tissue sections by seamlessly combining efficient cell lysis and robust cDNA amplification. In DRaqL, cells within fixed sections are efficiently lysed using a denaturing detergent, sodium deoxycholate (SDc). The denaturing activity of SDc is subsequently quenched by adding an excess amount of a non-denaturing detergent, Triton X-100, which allows efficient enzymatic reactions for cDNA amplification. The following protocol outlines the specific steps of DRaqL combined with Smart-seq2 (DRaqL-Smart-seq2), optimized for alcohol-fixed, dye-stained sections. Cells can be isolated from sections using laser capture microdissection (LCM) or any other device. The sensitivity of single-cell RNA-seq from murine ovarian sections with DRaqL-Smart-seq2 is comparable to that of deep RNA-seq of freshly dissociated single cells.1 This protocol can be adapted to formalin-fixed sections by incorporating protease treatment (DRaql-Protease-Smart-seq2), as noted in Steps 12 and 21–24. The protocol overview is illustrated in Figures 1 and 2.Figure 1Outline of LCM and cDNA amplificationFigure 2Outline of sequencing library preparation While this protocol focuses on Smart-seq2 for cDNA amplification, other cDNA amplification methods, namely SC3-seq2,3 and SMART-seq v4 3′DE Kit (Takara Bio, Z5040N), can also be combined with DRaqL.1 As outlined in Figure 3, the cDNA libraries are labeled with three different index sequences: in-line (IL) indexes incorporated in the reverse transcription primers (Oligo dT VN IL) (Step 12), and P5 and P7 indexes installed in PCR primers for sequencing libraries (Step 61). The IL index serves to distinguish 3′ ends of cDNAs from different cells, allowing the pooling of cDNAs after the first-strand synthesis (Step 29) or PCR amplification (Step 51).
